Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

aware adjective

also be aware of, be aware that, I’m aware, unaware, make aware, awareness

classical

Cic. Fam. 16.11.1: nōn ignōrō quantum ex dēsīderiō labōrēs

nōn ignōrāre

phrase: ignōrō, ignōrāre, ignōrāvī, ignōrātum with nōn, and an object, an accusative and infinitive or an indirect question

be aware (of, that)

Latin says “I am not unaware”: nōn ignōrō, and in the same way nōn sum nescius (Cic. Fam. 13.7.1). Plain sciō will often do (see know).

Other words

  • sentiō, sentīre, sēnsī, sēnsum — be aware of, sense, realise

    verb, fourth conjugation, transitive: with an object or an accusative and infinitive · also used · classical

    Awareness through the senses or the mind: to feel, to notice, to realise (see feel, notice). It also means to think, to hold an opinion (Lewis & Short).

  • gnārus, gnāra, gnārum — aware, knowing, acquainted with

    adjective: with the genitive, or an accusative and infinitive, declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 1.3.28 (Lewis & Short): nec locī gnāra sum; Cic. Brut. 228 (Lewis & Short): reī pūblicae

    Rare but classical (Lewis & Short), with the genitive of what one knows; its opposite ignārus, unaware, is common: ignārus sua sē tractāre perīcla (Ov. M. 8.195–200).

  • certiōrem facere — make aware, inform

    phrase: the person in the accusative (certiōrem, certiōrēs), the matter with dē or an accusative and infinitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.77.1: velim faciās eōs per litterās certiōrēs

    “To make someone more certain”: Cicero’s and Caesar’s phrase for informing someone. Passive certior fīō, I learn, I am told.

Examples

  • nōn ignōrō quantum ex dēsīderiō labōrēs; sed erunt omnia facilia sī valēbis.

    I’m well aware how much you suffer from missing us; but everything will be easy if you get well.Cic. Fam. 16.11.1

  • puer Īcarus ūnā stābat et, ignārus sua sē tractāre perīcla, ōre renīdentī modo, quās vaga mōverat aura, captābat plūmās

    the boy Icarus stood beside him and, unaware that he was handling his own doom, with a beaming face snatched at the feathers the wandering breeze had stirredOv. M. 8.195–200

See also know, notice, knowledge, understand, feel.
